standard_prerequisites.name: Over a locally Noetherian scheme all four notions of regular immersion agree and regularity can be checked on local rings, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the whole statement to a statement about the local rings at the three points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The composite of two regular immersions is a regular immersion, and the transitivity statement relating the conormal sequence of a composite to those of its factors, both cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the implications from the first condition to the second and from the second to the third.

standard_prerequisites.name: Any minimal sequence of generators of a quasi-regular ideal is a quasi-regular, hence regular, sequence, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes a minimal generating set of the ideal of the composite immersion a regular sequence.

standard_prerequisites.name: A minimal generating set of an ideal whose conormal sequence has a splitting compatible with a subideal can be chosen with the subideal's generators first, and a regular sequence splits into a regular sequence and a regular sequence modulo its first part
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the two shorter regular sequences that witness regularity of the individual immersions.

core_obligations: Reduce to local rings: on a locally Noetherian scheme the several notions of regular immersion coincide and regularity is checked at local rings, so the statement becomes a statement about the local rings of the three points (proof lines 5165-5168).

Record the known implications: regularity of both factors implies regularity of the composite, and regularity of the composite together with split exactness of the conormal sequence of the composite relative to the first factor implies the third condition, so only the converse of the last step is left (proof lines 5169-5173).

Set up the local algebra: write the ideals defining the two immersions inside the local ring of the outer point, note that any minimal generating sequence of the larger ideal is a regular sequence, and use the assumed split exactness of the displayed three-term sequence of conormal modules to choose a minimal generating system of the larger ideal whose first part minimally generates the smaller ideal (proof lines 5175-5187).

Split the regular sequence: the chosen sequence is regular by the previous step, and from the definition of a regular sequence it follows that its first part is a regular sequence in the outer local ring while the images of the remaining elements form a regular sequence modulo that first part; translating back, the second immersion is regular at the middle point and the first immersion is regular at the inner point (proof lines 5188-5197).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to local rings and note that two of the three implications are cited, leaving the third to be proved (proof lines 5165-5173).

Use the splitting of the conormal sequence to pick compatible minimal generators, get a regular sequence whose first part generates the smaller ideal, and split it to obtain regularity of the two factors (proof lines 5175-5197).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a composite of two immersions over a locally Noetherian base, regularity of both factors, regularity of the composite together with regularity of the first factor, and regularity of the composite together with split exactness of the conormal sequence are equivalent (statement lines 5144-5163). The counted proof is a compact local algebra argument: it reduces to local rings where all notions of regular immersion agree, cites two implications, and then proves the remaining one by choosing a minimal generating system of the larger ideal whose first part minimally generates the smaller ideal, using the assumed splitting, observing that this system is a regular sequence and splitting it according to the definition of a regular sequence to obtain the two shorter sequences (proof lines 5165-5197). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard criteria for regular sequences and conormal sequences.
